question.problem: If $f'(x)=|x+1|,$ sketch a possible graph of a continuous function $y=f(x).$
question.worked_solution:
The graph of $y=f'(x)$ is the following:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14200695/assets/57937f50c8adac57cd0a8b131ae2605466fe5e87e85ba324977a95b2f2c7a006.png)

Recall that critical points of $y=f(x)$ occur when $f'(x)=0$ or $f'(x)$ does not exist. In our case, there is one critical point: 

$\qquad$ $x=-1$ 

Also, we have the following: 

- If $f'(x) > 0$ then $f(x)$ is increasing.

- If $f'(x) <      0$ then $f(x)$ is decreasing.

We can now summarize the information from the graph in the table below.

| $x$ | $(-\infty,-1)$ | $-1$ | $(-1,\infty)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f'$ | $+$ | $0$ | $+$ |
| $f$ | $\nearrow$ | $\textrm{no extr.}$ | $\nearrow$ |

Let's now sketch the graph of $y=f(x)\mathbin{:}$

- First, we draw the critical point. We choose an arbitrary point on the vertical line $x=-1,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14200695/assets/296d0c0e63bedc37841aa914e0fb07320fff634ea1f6ac019a84cc47b87966b4.png)

- Next, we consider the behavior of $y=f(x)$ in the neighborhood of the critical points:

- Since $f(x)$ is increasing $\nearrow$ on $(-\infty,-1)$ and on $(-1,\infty)$, the graph of $y=f(x)$ goes down the left of $x=-1$ and goes up to the right of $x=-1.$

- Furthermore, since $f'(x)$ is decreasing to the left of $x = -1$, we must have $f''(x) <      0$, and, since it is increasing to the right of $x = -1$, we must have $f''(x) >    0.$ So, $x =-1$ is an inflection point at which the curve $y=f(x)$ changes from concave down to concave up.

So, we can draw as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14200695/assets/1c4fb55a07e1b55448ec2a2ada4fea07f363542cdf04a8676c90938b5c4f7fbe.png)

- Finally, since we are told that our graph must be continuous, by connecting and extending the existing parts with a smooth curve, we obtain a possible graph of $y=f(x)\mathbin{:}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14200695/assets/dfeb793809943dc496cc1f47b26f9b20aa3403b6d999787a7444ede605547226.png)
